memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Meanwhile, the Midianites sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officials, the captain of the guard." - Gen 37:36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter ends with a single quiet verse — and a single powerful word: "Meanwhile." While Jacob wept inconsolably at home, believing Joseph dead, something else was happening far away. Joseph was arriving in Egypt, being sold into the household of Potiphar, an official of Pharaoh. The story was not over. God was still writing it.

That word "meanwhile" is one of the most hopeful in the whole story. It reminds us that when everything looks like defeat, God is often already at work in ways we cannot see. To Jacob, this was the end — his son was gone. But to God, it was a beginning — Joseph was being placed exactly where he needed to be for a rescue that would one day save this whole family, and many nations besides, from famine.

Notice that Joseph did not land in Potiphar's house by accident. Through the cruelty of his brothers and the trade of merchants, God was sovereignly guiding Joseph's steps toward a purpose no one could yet imagine. What men meant for evil, God was already turning toward good (Gen 50:20).

Is there a "meanwhile" in your life — a place where you see only loss, while God is quietly at work behind the scenes? Take heart. Your story is not over. The same God who was with Joseph in Egypt is with you, working all things together for good for those who love Him (Rom 8:28).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I see only loss, while God may be at work behind the scenes?
2. Do I trust God's sovereign hand even in painful detours?
3. How does the word "meanwhile" bring hope to my situation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that when I see only loss, You are already at work "meanwhile." Help me to trust Your unseen hand, believing that You are working all things together for good. Amen.
